title: Advertising
subtitle: rock-bottom prices, pamper yourself, state-of-the-art
summary: Decode the language of advertising - the words that promise quality, value, luxury, scientific backing and beauty - and name the ways products are advertised.

lesson.heading: Promoting quality
lesson.text: Advertisers like language that suggests their product is of especially high quality. **Innovative** means original and interesting; **unsurpassed** means the best there is. To **leave others standing** is to be much better than them, and to **put** or **leave others in the shade** is to make them seem insignificant.

examples.text: Check out our latest smartphone - you'll love its **innovative** features.
The design of our beds is **unsurpassed**.
Our dishwashers **leave** other dishwashers **standing**.
Sign up for exam courses that **put other courses in the shade**.

lesson.heading: Promoting value for money
lesson.text: **Rock-bottom** prices are extremely low. If prices are **slashed**, they are dramatically reduced. **Galore** comes after the noun and means a huge number at ridiculously low prices, and a **discount** is a reduction in the price.

examples.text: **Rock-bottom** prices in our sale!
Prices **slashed**!
Bargains **galore**!
Order now and get a 10% **discount**.

lesson.note: Galore is unusual: it always follows the noun - bargains galore, not ~~galore bargains~~.

lesson.heading: Promoting luxury and comfort
lesson.text: To **pamper yourself** is to treat yourself to something luxurious; to **indulge yourself** is to let yourself have something you enjoy but which may be bad for you. **Sumptuous** and **opulent** both mean rich and special - sumptuous goes with food and furnishings, opulent with lifestyle and surroundings. To live **in the lap of luxury** is to live in a very luxurious way.

examples.text: **Pamper yourself** with a full-body massage.
**Indulge yourself** with our smooth, rich, perfectly blended coffee.
Enjoy a **sumptuous** meal in **opulent** surroundings.
Live **in the lap of luxury** for two weeks.

lesson.heading: Promoting scientific backing
lesson.text: **Ergonomically designed** means designed by studying people and their working or living conditions in order to improve effectiveness. **Medically proven** means shown by research, and **state-of-the-art** means using the very latest technology.

examples.text: This **ergonomically designed** reading lamp provides the perfect light.
Our health drink is **medically proven** to boost energy levels.
All our computers are **state-of-the-art**.

lesson.heading: Promoting attractiveness
lesson.text: To **stand out in the crowd** and to **turn heads** both mean to be noticed. **Tantalisingly** means temptingly, and **glossy** hair and **radiant** skin are both attractive and healthy-looking.

examples.text: Ties that will make you **stand out in the crowd**.
In our new styles, you're guaranteed to **turn heads**.
Our new lipsticks are **tantalisingly** appealing.
Use our range of products for **glossy** hair and **radiant** skin.

lesson.heading: Ways of advertising
rows: a very large advertising board, usually beside a road
a sheet of printed information, often handed out in the street
a brief excerpt from a film, TV or radio programme, used to advertise it
words written in the sky using smoke from a plane
posters hung at the back and front of a person who walks round a busy area
an advertisement that appears on your screen suddenly
an advertisement on TV or radio
a company's symbol, put on clothing and other products

lesson.heading: Plugging a product
lesson.text: Other common channels are magazine and newspaper **advertisements** (**adverts**, **ads**), **classified ads**, **posters**, **banners**, **sports sponsorship**, brochures and carrier bags. Celebrities often use TV interviews to **plug** a new book or film - that is, to advertise it.

examples.text: She went on TV to **plug** her new book.
My software is good at blocking **pop-up ads**.
There was a huge **billboard** advertising a new soft drink.

lesson.text: Pamper is pure treat; indulge suggests a small, pleasant sin - you pamper yourself with a massage, but you indulge yourself with chocolate.
